_comment: Single source of truth for which languages this translator handles and
where the parallel text lives. Every script reads this file, so adding a
language is a config change plus a data file -- no code edits.
To add a language:
1. Add it to `languages` (name = what appears in the prompt the model
is trained on, AND what the Learnut app sends to serve.py; code = a
short alias serve.py also accepts).
2. Add a corpus below naming its two columns.
3. Re-run prepare_data.py and retrain.
A corpus is either:
{ "file": "...", "columns": [A, B] }   one <sep>-delimited file, or
{ "dir":  "...", "columns": [A, B] }   an OPUS Moses folder (one
plain-text file per language).
Optional keys:
"limit": N         sample the corpus down to N pairs (a stable sample).
"train_only": true never used for validation/test. The default for Moses
folders: big downloaded corpora are there for fluency,
not to be scored on.
"synthetic": true  one side is machine-made (scripts/back_translate.py).
Emitted one way only, machine column -> human column.
`test` lists FROZEN test files: written to data/test.jsonl as they are and
kept out of training. Fill assets/test-taga-cuyo.txt once, with sentences a
native speaker translated, and never edit or train on it afterwards.
Pairs are emitted for every direction the data supports. A pair never
stated directly is still generated when both sides share one specific
translation in a third language, so bridging English in through Tagalog
yields English<->Cuyonon without translating Cuyonon twice.
ON THE REFERENCE CORPORA: the OPUS/HF sets under corpora/ are downloaded,
not committed (see .gitignore) -- they are large and their licences vary.
Every corpus is optional and skipped when missing. Each has a `limit`:
uncapped, the full download made Cuyonon 0.57% of the training data and
one epoch took ~10 days on a Colab T4. The base model already knows
English and Tagalog; a few thousand pairs keep that fluency without
drowning Cuyonon. prepare_data.py prints each language's share of the
training mix and warns when your own corpora fall below 30%. Tatoeba gets
the most room: short, clean, conversational, like the app's traffic.
Re-download with the URLs in scripts/mine_english.py if corpora/ is empty.
corpora/hf-tagalog-english comes from the Hugging Face dataset
rhyliieee/tagalog-filipino-english-translation (Apache-2.0, 105k rows),
converted by scripts/import_csv_corpus.py. Its rows are instruction-style
prompts whose Tagalog side appears machine-translated -- general fluency,
a poor match for short conversational phrases -- hence the small limit.
NOTE: Learnut sends the language NAME ('Tagalog', 'Cuyonon'), so
renaming a language here breaks the app until the app changes too.
serve.py accepts the name or the code, in any case.
